given: One image is open in single view. Its SegmentManager holds three segments whose class ids are [0, 0, 3]; class_aliases is {3: "stop sign"}; active_class_id is null (no class is toggled on in the class table); and the cached field next_class_id is 4, because _update_next_class_id ran after the last mutation and max({0,3}) + 1 = 4 (legacy/lazylabel/src/lazylabel/core/segment_manager.py:816-826). This state is per image and per viewer: opening another image calls clear(), which empties segments and class_aliases and resets next_class_id to 0, active_class_id to null and last_toggled_class_id to null (segment_manager.py:20-26, called from ui/managers/file_navigation_manager.py:281); multi-view keeps one independent SegmentManager per viewer (ui/managers/ai_segment_manager.py:339).
when: The user creates one new annotation through any single-view creation path that does not carry a class_id - accepting an AI mask (ai_segment_manager.py:283-284, building the dict at ui/main_window.py:1818-1829), finalizing a polygon (ui/managers/polygon_drawing_manager.py:201-206; ui/modes/single_view_mode.py:279-285), dragging a bounding box (ui/handlers/single_view_mouse_handler.py:426-432; single_view_mode.py:157-163) or dragging a circle (single_view_mouse_handler.py:517-525) - and then selects the pre-existing class-3 segment together with the new segment in the segment table and presses M ("Merge Selected Segments", config/hotkeys.py:83 -> main_window.py:1006 -> main_window.py:2000-2005 -> ui/managers/keyboard_event_manager.py:236-239 -> ui/managers/segment_table_manager.py:53-57 -> segment_manager.assign_segments_to_class).
then: Add: the incoming object has no "class_id" key, so add_segment fills one in (segment_manager.py:34). active_class_id is null, so the else branch applies and class_id = next_class_id = 4 (:38-39). last_toggled_class_id is set to 4 (:42), the segment is appended (:55), and only after the append is next_class_id recomputed (:56) to max({0,3,4}) + 1 = 5. Segments are now [0, 0, 3, 4] and next_class_id is 5. Merge: assign_segments_to_class([2, 3]) collects the non-null class ids of the selection, [3, 4], and takes their minimum, 3 (:70-77); it writes class 3 onto both selected segments (:81-83) and recomputes next_class_id (:85) over {0, 3} to max + 1 = 4. Final state: segments [0, 0, 3, 3], next_class_id back down to 4, active_class_id still null, last_toggled_class_id still 4 (assign_segments_to_class never touches it). Both merged segments now export under alias "stop sign", and the id 4 that was just handed out is free again and will be handed to the next unclassed annotation.
and: The order of checks in add_segment is exactly: (1) if the incoming object already has a class_id key, use its value verbatim and skip steps 2 and 3 - this holds even when the value is null (segment_manager.py:34); (2) otherwise, if active_class_id !== null, use active_class_id - the test is an explicit null check, not a truthiness check, so an active class 0 is honored (:36-37); (3) otherwise use the cached next_class_id (:38-39). Then always set last_toggled_class_id to the class actually used, defaulted or supplied (:42), append the segment (:55), and only then recompute next_class_id (:56). next_class_id is a cached field, never derived on demand at read time: _update_next_class_id runs after add (:56), delete (:63), assign/merge (:85), merge_segments_by_class (:172), reassign_class_ids (:391), and both erase paths - the erase paths only when at least one segment was actually modified (:581, :705). No other code writes class_id, so the cache is never stale. This is why the assigned id is annotation data and not a UI convenience: get_unique_class_ids() returns the sorted distinct ids (:87-95); every save path passes that list as class_order (ui/managers/save_export_manager.py:400 single view, :494 multi-view, main_window.py:6602); create_final_mask_tensor maps class_order[i] to output channel i and drops any segment whose id is not in the list (:221-223, :227-228); and class_labels is the alias of each id in the same order (save_export_manager.py:401-403, :495). core/exporters/npz.py:23-25 writes exactly that mask tensor, class_order and class_aliases. A different id therefore changes which channel a mask lands in, which name it is exported under, and whether two objects collapse into one class.
parameters: next_class_id = max({ s.class_id : s in segments, s.class_id !== null }) + 1, or 0 when that set is empty (segment_manager.py:816-826). Initial state and clear(): segments [], class_aliases {}, next_class_id 0, active_class_id null, last_toggled_class_id null (:13-26). active_class_id: int | null. toggle_active_class(id) always records last_toggled_class_id = id first, then clears active_class_id and returns false if it already equals id, otherwise sets it and returns true (:409-419); this toggle is reached only from the single-view class table (main_window.py:2699). set_active_class(id) assigns unconditionally and is what multi-view class clicks and the reassign flow use (:401-403; main_window.py:6446, 6456, 7211). Merge (assign_segments_to_class) target = min of the non-null class ids among the selected indices, else next_class_id when the selection has none (:70-79); an empty index list returns immediately and recomputes nothing (:67-68); indices past the end of the list are skipped (:73, :82). reassign_class_ids(new_order) builds id_map = {new_order[i]: i}, rewrites every segment whose id is a key of that map (:379-382), then rebuilds class_aliases as {id_map[old]: alias} for old ids that currently have an alias, which drops aliases for ids absent from new_order (:385-390), and finally recomputes next_class_id (:391). new_order comes from the class table, which lists only ids that have segments, in the user's drag order (ui/right_panel.py:361-371 via segment_table_manager.py:96-100).
edgeCases: Empty image: with no segments next_class_id is 0, so the first new annotation gets class 0 (segment_manager.py:823-824; pinned by tests/unit/core/test_segment_manager.py:108-119).

Active class 0 must be honored: the guard is active_class_id !== null, not a truthiness test (segment_manager.py:36). A TypeScript port written as `if (activeClassId)` would wrongly start a new class whenever class 0 is active.

The default fires only when the class_id key is ABSENT (segment_manager.py:34). An explicit class_id of null is preserved as null; such a segment is skipped by _update_next_class_id (:819-822) and dropped from every export because its id is not in class_order (:227-228, :91-93).
Gaps are never filled by this rule: ids {0, 3} give 4, not 1; ids {0, 4} give 5 (segment_manager.py:826).

next_class_id can go DOWN and ids are reused: with classes {0, 1, 4}, deleting every class-4 segment leaves max 1, so next_class_id becomes 2 (delete_segments :58-63 then :826). It also goes down after a merge, as in the worked example above (5 back to 4).

Alias leak on id reuse (likely defect): delete_segments and assign_segments_to_class never prune class_aliases - only clear() (:23) and reassign_class_ids (:385-390) touch it. With classes {0, 3} and alias {3: "stop sign"}, deleting every class-3 segment sets next_class_id to 1; the next three new annotations get 1, 2, then 3 - and that third one silently inherits the name "stop sign" in exports (save_export_manager.py:401-403, :495).

Reassign Class IDs renumbers the in-use classes to 0..n-1 in class-table order (segment_manager.py:375-391). It does NOT update active_class_id, so after a reassign the active class can point at a different class or at one that no longer exists. The `str(old_id)` fallback at :386 is unreachable dead code, guarded out by `if old_id in self.class_aliases` at :388 - do not port it as a behavior.

Merge (M) does NOT use the active class, despite the docstrings at keyboard_event_manager.py:237 and segment_manager.py:66 saying so. It uses the minimum of the selected segments' ids (:77), and only falls back to next_class_id when none of the selected segments has a non-null id (:79).
Aliases never reserve ids: _update_next_class_id reads segments only (segment_manager.py:818-822), so a named class with no segments does not hold its number.

Multi-view AI accept duplicates the active-else-next logic in the CALLER and then sets class_id explicitly, so add_segment's own default is bypassed (ai_segment_manager.py:366-371; main_window.py:6879-6885). Each viewer uses its own manager, so in linked mode with no active class the two viewers pick ids independently and can diverge.

Linked polygon finalize is the one exception: a single shared id is computed from the primary viewer BEFORE finalizing and passed to both viewers (main_window.py:5619-5650, 6990-7006). Multi-view bbox and circle set no class_id and fall through to add_segment's per-viewer default (main_window.py:5815, 5909).
"Click the same class again to deactivate" is single-view only: multi-view class clicks call set_active_class, not toggle_active_class (main_window.py:6446, 6456 vs :2699).
active_class_id is never validated against existing classes and is not cleared when its last segment is deleted, so a new annotation can join a class that currently has no segments.

Load paths cannot be affected: every NPZ/JSON/annotation load passes an explicit class_id (core/file_manager.py:259, 273, 324, 403, 590, 672, 701), so a file whose highest id is 250 simply leaves next_class_id at 251 after the last add_segment recompute (:56).
Annotation IMPORT uses a DIFFERENT allocator - the lowest free id not already taken by an alias or by a numeric label (file_manager.py:370-377) - and must not share an implementation with this rule.

Undo/redo never triggers the default: undo of an add calls delete_segments, which recomputes (core/undo_redo_manager.py:155), and redo re-adds the saved dict, which already carries class_id (:367, :373, :591, :597, :647, :652). AI-to-polygon conversion also preserves class_id (segment_manager.py:882, :900).
answer: Answered: yes, this rule guards annotation data integrity, and the approver restored it to P0 on 2026-09-17 - the id assigned here IS the id written to every export. get_unique_class_ids() returns the sorted distinct ids (segment_manager.py:87-95); every save path hands that list to create_final_mask_tensor as class_order (save_export_manager.py:400, :494; main_window.py:6602); the function maps class_order[i] to output channel i and silently drops any segment whose id is missing from the list (segment_manager.py:221-223, :227-228); and the parallel class_labels list is the alias of each id in the same order (save_export_manager.py:401-403, :495), which npz.py:23-25 persists alongside the mask. So reusing an existing id merges two distinct objects into one channel, and choosing a different free id shifts every higher class's channel and changes the exported name - the compliance judges' "the user can see and fix it" argument does not survive the fact that the save happens without re-validating the id. Three things in the card were wrong. (1) The When/Then were internally inconsistent: the Given establishes classes {0, 3}, so after the add the classes are {0, 3, 4} and there is no class 5 to select; the corrected example selects the class-3 and class-4 segments and lands on 3 via min() at segment_manager.py:77. (2) The Then ended on the vague phrase "recalculated as the highest remaining class + 1" instead of a number; it is 4, because _update_next_class_id runs over the post-merge set {0, 3} (segment_manager.py:85, :816-826). (3) The parameters line "next_class_id = max(existing ids) + 1; 0 when empty" omitted that the None-valued ids are filtered out (:819-822) and, more importantly, that next_class_id is a CACHED field recomputed only at :56, :63, :85, :172, :391, :581 and :705 - an implementer who derives it lazily on read will diverge on the erase paths, which recompute only when modified_indices is non-empty. The card also duplicated an edge case ("gaps are never reused" twice, lines 18 and 20) and stated "deleting all class-4 segments makes the next new class 2" without the surrounding classes that make it true. What an implementer must watch for: the active-class test is `!== null`, not truthiness, so class 0 works as an active class (:36); the default applies only when the class_id KEY is absent, not when its value is null (:34); the id is picked BEFORE the append and the recompute, so the new segment's own id never influences its own assignment (:39, :55-56); merge ignores the active class despite its docstring (keyboard_event_manager.py:237); next_class_id can go down and ids are reused, and because delete never prunes class_aliases (only :23 and :385-390 do) a reused id silently inherits the old class name in exports; reassign_class_ids does not update active_class_id (:375-391); multi-view keeps one manager per viewer and reimplements the fallback in the caller (ai_segment_manager.py:366-369; main_window.py:6879-6882), except for linked polygon finalize which shares one id (main_window.py:5619-5630); and the annotation-import allocator at file_manager.py:370-377 is a different algorithm (lowest free id not taken by an alias) that must not be folded into this one.
corrections: Fixed the contradictory When: the card selected "classes 3 and 5" but its own Given plus the add produces classes {0, 3, 4}; there is no class 5. Now selects the class-3 and class-4 segments.
Made the Then concrete end-to-end with real numbers: 4 assigned, next_class_id 5, merge target min(3,4)=3, next_class_id recomputed to 4 (segment_manager.py:39, :56, :77, :85, :826).
Stated the exact order of checks in add_segment (key present -> active_class_id !== null -> next_class_id) and that the id is chosen before the append and before the recompute (:34-39, :55-56).
Added that the active-class guard is an explicit null check, so class 0 is a valid active class, and that a truthiness port is wrong (:36).

Added that the default applies only when the class_id key is absent, not when its value is null, and that a null id is skipped by the next-id computation and dropped from export (:34, :819-822, :227-228).

Corrected the parameters: the id set excludes null values, and next_class_id is a cached field recomputed at :56, :63, :85, :172, :391, :581, :705 - the erase recomputes being conditional on modified_indices.
Added the last_toggled_class_id side effect of add_segment (:42) and of toggle_active_class (:412), which the card omitted entirely.

Corrected the plain-English claim about merge: it is triggered by M via keyboard_event_manager.py:236-239 -> assign_segments_to_class, and it uses min of the selected ids, NOT the active class, contradicting the docstrings at keyboard_event_manager.py:237 and segment_manager.py:66.
Deduplicated the two identical "gaps are never reused" edge cases (card lines 18 and 20) into one.
Made "deleting all class-4 segments makes the next new class 2" well-formed by naming the starting classes {0, 1, 4}.

Corrected the reordering edge case: reassign_class_ids remaps aliases from old id to new index and drops aliases whose id is absent from new_order; it does not "drop classes that had no alias". Also flagged the unreachable str(old_id) fallback at :386 and that active_class_id is not remapped.

Replaced the vague "each multi-view viewer computes its own next ID" with the actual mechanics: one manager per viewer, the fallback duplicated in the caller and set explicitly (ai_segment_manager.py:366-371; main_window.py:6879-6885), linked polygon finalize sharing one id (main_window.py:5619-5650, 6990-7006), and multi-view bbox/circle falling through to the per-viewer default (main_window.py:5815, 5909).
Added that multi-view class clicks use set_active_class, so the click-again-to-deactivate toggle is single-view only (main_window.py:6446, 6456 vs :2699).
Added the alias-leak edge case with a worked sequence, and the fact that aliases never reserve ids.

Added that every load path passes an explicit class_id (file_manager.py:259, 273, 324, 403, 590, 672, 701) and that annotation import uses a different allocator (file_manager.py:370-377) that must stay separate.
Added the undo/redo and AI-to-polygon-conversion paths as cases where the default never fires and the cache stays correct (undo_redo_manager.py:155, :367, :373; segment_manager.py:882, :900).

Added the export chain to the And clause so the P0 justification is testable from the card alone (segment_manager.py:87-95, :221-223; save_export_manager.py:400-403, :494-495; exporters/npz.py:23-25).

Extended the source list beyond the card's four ranges to the call sites that actually reach the rule: main_window.py:1818-1829, 2000-2005, 5619-5650, 5815, 5909, 6879-6885, 6990-7006; ai_segment_manager.py:283-284, 339, 366-371; keyboard_event_manager.py:236-239; segment_table_manager.py:53-57; polygon_drawing_manager.py:201-206; single_view_mouse_handler.py:426-432, 517-525; single_view_mode.py:157-163, 279-285; file_navigation_manager.py:281.
unresolved: Two product-owner calls, both outside the scope of a faithful port. (1) Alias reuse: because delete_segments never prunes class_aliases (segment_manager.py:58-63; only :23 and :385-390 touch the table), an id that is freed and later re-handed-out silently inherits the deleted class's name and exports under it (save_export_manager.py:401-403, :495). The contract above preserves this legacy behavior, but the owner should say whether it is intended or a defect to fix in the rewrite. (2) Linked multi-view inconsistency: an AI accept picks a class id independently per viewer (ai_segment_manager.py:366-369), while a linked polygon finalize shares one id computed from the primary viewer (main_window.py:5619-5630, 6990-7006), so the same user gesture can yield matching or diverging ids depending on the tool used. The owner should decide which of the two is the intended contract.
